prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of a handmade zine cover sitting on a cheap plywood table under a single overhead fluorescent light, long faint drum-line streaks visible across the paper. The background outside the zine is dim and irrelevant. The zine is photocopied onto grey newsprint-like paper with a thin center staple that is slightly off-center.

Subject:
The master cover sets the identity of this zine: a single large torn-magazine strip forming the main subject, three cut-out magazine letters at wildly different sizes making a wordlike shape, a scissor-fray border along the entire perimeter, a yellow highlighter circle around a hand-drawn asterisk, and a cement-glue halo around the biggest torn piece.

Important details:
This image defines the zine's palette (grey newsprint, highlighter yellow, ballpoint blue, tomato red marker) and every subsequent spread must reuse the same stock and the same cut-out letter aesthetic. Every torn edge must be physically irregular. Glue halos must be translucent yellow-brown, not digital. The composition should read as a cover without being symmetrical.

Use case:
Reference image 1 of 4 for the One Zine Issue series. Later spreads will preserve the exact paper stock, glue halos, marker palette, and cut-out letter style.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names on any torn scrap, no vector edges, no sharp digital crispness, no symmetry, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.

description: The reference cover of a handmade photocopy zine, establishing paper stock, glue halos, cut-out letter style, and marker palette.
